title: Meta is offering $1 billion for you to feel better about data centers
excerpt: You can tell people AI data centers are good for them and they may never believe you. But a $1 billion check from Mark Zuckerberg might persuade them.
content_html:
Mark Zuckerberg is trying to solve his AI data center problem with a $1 billion giveaway

By Peter Kafka

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Chief Correspondent covering media and technology

Last month, Meta launched an "AI is good, really" PR campaign. My response: Words are fine, but why not cut people checks?

On Monday, Meta announced it's taking my (free) advice: It says it will create a $1 billion fund to boost communities where it is building AI data centers.

There's very little public detail about the fund. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg mentions it briefly in a long memo explaining (again) why "The Future is for Everyone" (the memo literally recycles lines from a WSJ op-ed Zuckerberg published last month called "The AI Future is for Everyone").

There's no mention of how many communities or people this is meant to help, or over what period the money is meant to be spent. But a person familiar with the plan tells me the idea is to spend the money in addition to the investments Meta is making directly in its data centers.

That would be different from what happened in rural Richland Parish, Louisiana, where teachers are getting a one-time bonus of up to $50,000 because of a Meta data center: That money is coming from a tax bill Meta paid in conjunction with its construction costs. Writing a check directly to communities and the people who live there, over and above what Meta spends on data center construction, staffing, and taxes, seems like money well spent.

And it's definitely money Meta can afford. Last year, the company reported profits of $60 billion.

None of which means this will work. There is deep-seated anger, mistrust, and fear about data centers (I highly recommend the recent reporting about communities responding to data centers in Michigan and Wisconsin by journalist Jasmine Sun). There are also deep-seated bad vibes about Zuckerberg and Meta in particular, and about Big Tech in general.

And there's also the fact that social networks — the products that give Zuckerberg and Meta the money to invest billions in data centers — are the same products that make it easier for people to organize against the data centers. And which can also be blamed for people being dubious of… everything.

As technology columnist Max Read puts it: "The low-trust environment cultivated over the past couple decades by the tech industry's flagship companies has now created real obstacles to its ambitions. Now that tech giants are the institutions—and effectively in charge of US industrial policy—they are getting a first-hand lesson in how corrosive to long-term planning institutional mistrust can be."

But again: While AI can be legitimately scary for lots of reasons, almost all of them have to do with what might happen, one day. Putting cash in people's pockets today may be the best tool the tech guys have. And they have plenty of cash to spare.

content_html_zh:
马克·扎克伯格正试图通过 10 亿美元的赠品来解决他的人工智能数据中心问题

作者：Peter Kafka 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 媒体和科技首席记者

上个月，Meta 发起了一场“人工智能真的很好”的公关活动。 我的回答：话虽好，但为什么不削减人员支票呢？

周一，Meta 宣布采纳我的（免费）建议：它将设立一个 10 亿美元的基金，以促进正在建设人工智能数据中心的社区的发展。

关于该基金的公开细节很少。 Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格在一份长篇备忘录中简短地提到了这一点（再次）解释为什么“未来属于每个人”（该备忘录实际上是引用了扎克伯格上个月发表的《华尔街日报》专栏文章《人工智能的未来属于每个人》中的台词）。

没有提及这将帮助多少社区或人民，也没有提及这笔钱将在多长时间内使用。 但一位熟悉该计划的人士告诉我，这个想法是除了 Meta 直接在其数据中心进行的投资之外，还要花这笔钱。

这与路易斯安那州里奇兰教区农村地区发生的情况不同，那里的教师因 Meta 数据中心而获得高达 50,000 美元的一次性奖金：这笔钱来自 Meta 与其建设成本一起支付的税单。 直接向社区和居住在那里的人们开一张支票，除了 Meta 在数据中心建设、人员配备和税收上的支出之外，似乎这笔钱花得值。

这绝对是 Meta 能够负担得起的钱。 去年，该公司报告利润为 600 亿美元。

这些都不意味着这会起作用。 人们对数据中心存在根深蒂固的愤怒、不信任和恐惧（我强烈推荐记者 Jasmine Sun 最近关于密歇根州和威斯康星州数据中心的社区响应的报道）。 人们还对扎克伯格和 Meta 以及一般的大型科技公司抱有根深蒂固的不良情绪。

还有一个事实是，社交网络——这些产品为扎克伯格和梅塔提供了数十亿美元的资金投资数据中心——也让人们更容易组织起来反对数据中心。 这也可以归咎于人们怀疑…… 一切。

正如科技专栏作家马克斯·里德（Max Read）所说：“科技行业的旗舰公司在过去几十年里营造的低信任环境现在为其雄心壮志制造了真正的障碍。 现在，科技巨头成为了机构，并且有效地负责美国的产业政策，他们正在得到第一手的教训，了解机构不信任对长期规划的破坏性有多大。”

但再次强调：虽然人工智能可能因多种原因而令人恐惧，但几乎所有原因都与有一天可能发生的事情有关。 如今，将现金放入人们的口袋可能是科技人员拥有的最好工具。 而且他们还有大量闲置现金。
